The spec also requires the metastability model: spec:181 REQ-VER-001 "every bit of a synchronizer is modelled independently ... the model shall apply a random latency, chosen independently for each bit and each change" (DEC-012, rules.json:10323). spec:684 claims "A Gray pointer changes one bit per update, so a late bit makes the destination domain see the previous pointer value". spec:1246 TEST-008 asks for "flags never optimistic" with the model enabled. contract.json:560 says CHK-014 is meant to run with the model off.
analyses.rtl_does: m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv:120 w_occ = reg_wbin - w_rbin_s, and :126 o_full_thr = w_wr_blk ? (i_full_thr==0) : (w_occ >= i_full_thr). :106 o_full = exact Gray compare with MSBs inverted. If o_full_thr=1 while o_full=0 with no block, w_occ is in 9..15. A real pointer pair cannot give that, so the synchronized read pointer w_rbin_s (from u_sync_rd_gray, :233-242) does not match any value the read pointer actually had. The cause is the sim branch of m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:149-182. Each bit has its own random extra delay (:158-169, sim_extra 0..2), and o_q = sim_cur when the model is enabled (:182). In base.s1 this test ran with i_clk_wr 14 ns and i_clk_rd 6 ns (base.s1.log:47), so the read Gray pointer changes several bits between write edges. A later bit with delay 0 can then appear before an earlier bit with delay 1-2, which gives a non-adjacent Gray value. The SVA a_CHK_013 (nnc_chk_wr.sv:112-117) independently reports fails=4 in base.s1 and fails=5 in small.s1 but 0 in model_off.s1 and syn.s1 (logs: base.s1.log:8822, model_off.s1.log:21801, syn.s1.log:21790).
analyses.test_does: test_async_gray_fifo.py:846-891. It sets ft=DEPTH, et=0 and picks clocks 10/14 or 14/6 (:850). It cannot turn the model off and only logs not_verifiable when !EXACT (:856-857). It writes one word, fills to 8, reads one, then drains (:891). The always-on monitor _on_w (:188-202) computes exp = int(full==1 and sw==1 and busy==0) at :201 and asserts fth == exp at :202, which is exactly contract CHK-013(c).

candidates.evidence_for: The RTL model follows REQ-VER-001/DEC-012 to the letter: per-bit independent delay of 0..2, and the pending change is replaced on a new input (spec:181, spec:653, rules.json:10323). The spec claims this only makes the destination see the 'previous pointer value' (spec:684). That holds only when Gray updates are farther apart than the delay window, which is true in the spec demo (bits 'six source cycles apart', spec:653). With fast source clocks, several bits change within the window and the per-bit delays reorder them. The spec does not say how to reconcile this with REQ-FUNC-008/009 and TEST-008 'flags never optimistic'. The failure appears only with +AFIFO_MSYNC_EN=1 and passes with the model off and with VLSIT_SYNTHESIS.
candidates.evidence_against: One can argue the spec's intent (spec:684-685: 'the model is there to check that the FIFO flags stay pessimistic when a bit arrives late') clearly forbids non-sequential values. That would make the model implementation, not the spec, the defect.

candidates.evidence_for: The model deliverable (m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:149-182) produces synchronized vectors that a real 2-FF synchronizer could not produce. Real metastability affects only the bit that is changing at the sampling edge, and it resolves to the old or new value. The resulting optimistic estimate violates REQ-FUNC-008 at the DUT ports. The design logic itself (wr.sv:106-126) is correct for legal Gray inputs, as model_off and syn show.
candidates.evidence_against: The RTL does exactly what REQ-VER-001/DEC-012 require: independent per bit and per change. The flag logic in m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv is correct whenever the synchronized pointer is a legal Gray value.

candidates.evidence_for: contract.json:560 says CHK-014 is for 'Metastability model off', but the test still runs in model-on builds (:856-857 only logs not_verifiable).
candidates.evidence_against: The failing assertion is not a CHK-014 latency check. It is the always-on CHK-013(c) consistency check (:200-202), which matches contract.json:524 exactly. The independent SVA a_CHK_013 fires on the same runs. CHK-013 is required in every configuration.

analyses.options: (1) Clarify the spec (REQ-VER-001/DEC-012, §10.6.4): state that the model must keep the order of Gray bit changes so the destination only sees source values (old or newer, in order). For example, require that a bit's delayed change is never overtaken by a later change of another bit, or apply one delay per crossing/update instead of per bit. Alternatively, explicitly limit the extra delay so it cannot exceed the spacing of source updates. Then fix the RTL model in m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:149-182 to match (this needs the per-bit wrapper to be told about ordering, or the model moved/extended into m_vlsit_afifo_sync, which REQ-VER-001/DEC-039 currently forbid). (2) If the requester keeps the current model, the spec must say that flags may be optimistic with the model on, which contradicts REQ-FUNC-008/009 and TEST-008. That needs a requester decision, not a test change. Do not relax CHK-013.
